page: Vultr vx1-g-32c-128g-1920s is a general-purpose server belonging to the VX1 Cloud Compute family. It features 32 dedicated vCPUs powered by an AMD EPYC processor with an x86_64 architecture, 16 physical cores, and 2 threads per core operating at 2.0 GHz. The processor includes a cache hierarchy of 48 KB L1d, 1.0 MB L2, and 32 MB L3 cache. It is equipped with 128.0 GB of system memory, providing a balanced 4.0 GB of RAM per core. Storage is bundled with a 1920 GB local NVMe SSD, and the server includes one complimentary public IPv4 address. No GPU accelerators are present.

Benchmark results indicate top-tier single-core performance, with stress-ng single-core CPU performance, Geekbench single-core score, and single-threaded compression and decompression all ranking in the top 10%. Multi-core performance is strong, with Geekbench multi-core and PassMark CPU scores placing in the top 25%, though stress-ng multi-core performance falls in the middle 50%. Memory performance is highly efficient, highlighted by a top-tier PassMark memory score and top-tier large-block write bandwidth of 194.79 GB/sec. Large-block read bandwidth is also strong at 295.05 GB/sec.

The server demonstrates strong capabilities in database operations and text processing, with PassMark database operations and Redis SET operations ranking in the top 25%. For AI workloads, CPU-based LLM inference is highly capable for smaller models, achieving top-tier prompt processing and text generation speeds with a 135M model, and strong text generation speeds with larger 7B and 70B models, though prompt processing for larger models remains average. The hardware supports advanced instruction sets including AVX-512, VNNI, and cryptography acceleration, which aids in secure data processing and vector calculations.

Given the dedicated AMD EPYC cores, high-capacity NVMe SSD, and 128 GB RAM, this server offers a balanced resource density suitable for production workloads. It is well-suited for relational and NoSQL databases, static web serving, text and image processing pipelines, and moderate LLM inference tasks. The lack of a GPU limits its utility for heavy deep learning training, but its strong single-core performance and fast local storage make it an efficient choice for general-purpose enterprise applications and data-intensive services.
